context: Heuristic lint checks, not execution: e.g. a rung whose expected-text declares gating ('exits 1 on an unfixed tree') gets structural scrutiny; a source file in only_modify whose conventional test file exists on disk but is not in scope is a finding. Keep false-positive cost low: warn-level findings, and items whose work legitimately touches no tests stay createable.
description: Successor of todo-lint-rung-falsifiability-and-scope-completeness (dropped 2026-07-31: its rung 2, `pytest tests/unit/scripts/test_todo_db_v2.py -q -k lint`, already passes on the unfixed tree - 6 existing lint tests pass - so it verified nothing about the coverage it claimed; a non-gating rung on the item that is about non-gating rungs). Premise (re-validated 2026-07-31): `todo lint` returns 0 findings on every currently open item, yet audit found gating defects in five of them: rungs green on the unfixed tree, prose-placeholder rungs, and only_modify sets omitting the test file the item's own work units promise. lint should (a) flag rungs whose EXPECTED text claims failure on the unfixed tree but whose semantics cannot gate (heuristics; running arbitrary rung commands at lint time is out of scope), and (b) flag only_modify sets that name a source file with an existing test file while omitting that test file. Depends on todo-lint-unrunnable-verification-commands-2: the falsifiability signal is vacuously satisfiable by a broken (unrunnable) rung, so brokenness rejection must land first.

preserves.behavior: Existing lint findings keep firing unchanged
Items whose work legitimately touches no tests are not made un-createable
